## Purpose

Owner outcome: "Help a Grade 11 learner distinguish instantaneous velocity from acceleration and transfer the idea to a new motion problem."
Design strategy: "Use the concrete unresolved question; reuse existing work and keep conditional future work distinct."
This step: "Address the specific misconception with transparent reasoning."
- O-CONTENT: "Create correct scaffolded material."; done when: "Worked reasoning, misconception contrast and meaningful transfer assessment."

## Deliverable

"Draft one short learner-facing explanation of the stipulated upward throw through the turning instant, with a separate reviewer calculation note and a held-at-rest contrast."
Assignment support: GUIDED
Method: "Draft one short learner-facing explanation of the stipulated upward throw through the turning instant, with a separate reviewer calculation note and a held-at-rest contrast."
Required understanding:
- "Zero instantaneous velocity does not imply zero acceleration."
- "Instantaneous quantities, signed acceleration, prerequisites and transfer: Needed to interpret the concrete case and its limits."
Thinking operations: ["derive", "construct"]
Profiles: ["Purpose and uncertainty", "Learning and transfer", "Quantities and assumptions"]

## Authoritative inputs

- S-TEACHER [SYNTHETIC/SUPPLIED] "case.md" revision null; "Synthetic Grade 11 kinematics brief; no board syllabus or real learner assessment supplied."
Declared context (conditions retained):
- C-CLAIMS [CONSTRAINT/CURRENT] "Do not claim learning gains without actual learner evidence."
- C-PHYSICS [CONSTRAINT/CURRENT] "Use the declared one-dimensional constant-gravity model and explicit signs/units."
  Condition: "For this example only: initial upward velocity 18 m/s, upward positive, g=9 m/s^2, no drag."
- F-PREREQ [FACT/CURRENT] "The synthetic learner knows displacement and velocity but confuses zero velocity with zero acceleration."
- R-LEARN [REQUIREMENT/CURRENT] "Teach and assess the velocity/acceleration distinction, not formula copying."
